GET TO KNOW YOUR SETUP

Good signals start here.

Match the receiver and antenna to what you want to hear.

Choose your RTL-SDR

Choose your model to see its connector and receive range.

The browser receiver supports 25–1750 MHz. Your tuner's actual range may be narrower.

Give your antenna a clear view

Start near a window, away from computers, chargers, and metal obstructions. A band-matched antenna can make a bigger difference than more gain.

Weather & local FM
A vertical VHF antenna is a good starting point.
Airband
Use an antenna designed for approximately 118–137 MHz.
Weak or noisy signal
Move the antenna first. Then adjust gain and squelch.

The 1.14.0 radio core, in your browser

Live listening, precision Hz tuning, channel plans, nearby station discovery, and exact favorites are available here. ADS-B aircraft tracking, propagation guidance, Morse text decoding, and band surveys remain native-app features.

CONNECTED, LOCALLY

Bring your SDR online.

A small local bridge connects your browser to the PC's USB driver.

First run on Windows

  1. Connect your RTL-SDR.

    Install the WinUSB driver for the SDR interface using the official Nooelec setup guide ↗.

  2. Build the local radio core.

    From the downloaded project folder, with Python and a C build tool installed:

    python scripts/build-web-core.py
  3. Start the local bridge.python web/bridge/server.py

    Open the local address printed by the bridge, then select Detect receiver.

Detailed platform setup and requirements are in the project's web README. Keep the bridge running while listening.

Why a local bridge?

Browsers cannot load the PC's serial or USB drivers directly. The bridge uses the native RTL-SDR driver for radio processing and streams audio and spectrum data to this page.

RTL-SDR radios use USB, not a serial port. Web Serial does not provide RTL-SDR reception.

Optional USB identification

In supported browsers, identify a connected USB device using the browser's permission picker. This does not start reception or replace the bridge.

Your audio stays on this computer

The receiver runs through the bridge on localhost. Nearby ZIP lookup uses an external location service; the station catalog is bundled with the app. A tab that is hidden pauses its spectrum updates while audio can continue.
